cases.reason: Both meet every criterion, but Y hands over a ready-to-print adapted worksheet for the whole class, which saves the most preparation the night before.
Both rewrites are accurate and pitched well, but X adds headings, a glossary, comprehension questions and a clear note of changes, while Y gives only a one-line note.

Y is a single student-facing sheet with error codes, a labelled model paragraph and code-matched tasks, while X is a longer lesson package whose spelling tip ('response' + 'ability') would push students towards misspelling responsibility.

Y runs a little long at 30 to 35 minutes, but its French is correct throughout and it gives full answers and a parent answer strip, while X's student writing frame wrongly offers 'as' for the third person.
